newsitem.title: USA: Gensia to buy three drug companies.
newsitem.headline: Gensia to buy three drug companies.

text.p: Gensia Inc said it will acquire three pharmaceutical companies as part of a plan to create a vertically integrated specialty pharmaceutical company focusing on the worldwide oncology and injectable pharmaceutical markets.

The companies it will buy by issuing 29.5 million new shares are SICOR SpA, a Milan-based supplier of specialty bulk pharmaceuticals; Sintesis Lerma SA de CV, a supplier of specialty bulk pharmaceuticals based in Mexico; and Lemery SA de CV, a multi-source pharmaceutical company based in Mexico with sales to central and south America and Eastern Europe.
The combined company will be called Gensia Sicor Inc and will be based in San Diego. It will be one of only a few vertically integrated supplers of chemotherapy drugs for the cancer market.

Gensia said SICOR, Lerma and Lemery had aggregate sales of $60.7 million in 1995 and $36.4 million in the first six months of this year. Ths compares with Gensia's total sales of $53.5 million last year and $25.7 million for the first six months of 1996.
Gensia said the deal, subject to shareholder approval and other conditions, is expected to close by April of 1997.
Gensia Inc said it will spin off certain research and development programs into a newly formed public comany to be called Metabasis Therapeutics Inc.
It said shares of the new company will be distributed to Gensia shareholders immediately prior to completion of its planned acquisition of three pharmaceutical firms.
Gensia said it expects Metabasis may be supported in part by payments from outside research collaborations and from "potential additional financings."
It said its collaboration with Pfizer Inc for the treatment of pain, may be contributed to Metabasis, subject to Pfizer approval.

Gensia also said it is planning to transfer all of its medical device assets including the Laryngeal Mask Airway, the GenESA(R) System and the Feedback Controlled Heparin System into a wholly-owned subsidiary to be called Gensia Automedics Inc.
Gensia said it plans to explore private and public financing for Gensia Automedics, subject to certain third party consents.
